content: 1. The intrauterine devices (IUDs) Liletta and Mirena are approved for the management of heavy menstrual bleeding for up to five years in women who choose intrauterine contraception as their contraceptive method. The initial release rate of levonorgestrel from the 52-mg intrauterine system is approximately 20–21 mcg/day, which decreases by about 50% after five years. Replacement of the device is recommended after the fifth year if continued treatment is required. 2. No studies have been conducted to evaluate the effects of renal or hepatic impairment on the use of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems. 3. The combination of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems with antithrombin alfa or antithrombin III may result in pharmacodynamic antagonism, reducing the effects of either drug. This combination should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 4. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. The combination of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems with argatroban, bemiparin, bivalirudin, dalteparin, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, or heparin may result in pharmacodynamic antagonism, reducing the effects of either drug. Avoid these combinations or use alternative drugs due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Levonorgestrel intrauterine systems may decrease the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Women should be advised to use nonhormonal contraceptives during elagolix treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 9. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Women of childbearing potential should use highly effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after the last dose of encorafenib. 10. Sugammadex sodium may decrease the effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by receptor binding competition. If a hormonal contraceptive is used on the same day as sugammadex, additional nonhormonal contraception should be used for the next seven days. 11. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Perampanel decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Levonorgestrel levels are reduced by 40% when coadministered with high-dose perampanel (12 mg/day). Backup contraception is recommended. 14. Levonorgestrel intrauterine systems may decrease the effects of insulin (including insulin degludec, insulin aspart, and inhaled insulin) by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Use caution and monitor glucose levels. 15. Levonorgestrel intrauterine systems decrease the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives have been shown to significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. 16. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse reactions. 17. Levonorgestrel intrauterine systems increase the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 18. Levonorgestrel intrauterine systems decrease the effects of metformin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glucose levels. 19. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and consider nonhormonal contraception. 20. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 21. Teriflunomide increases the levels of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 22. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 23. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects.
